description: The template's design, your data, your words. `knobs` are the template's settings (get_template shows the schema): theme light|dark|editorial, dataType gradient|buckets|categories and surroundings true|false (then waterColor, landColor) for maps, title/description/source/brand {text, fontFamily, fontSize, color}, backgroundColor, and the scale knobs for the dataType (colormap and direction, range, breaks or classes, categoryColors/categoryOrder). data = {columns: [{id, type}], rows: [[…]]}: use the template's column ids, or exactly two columns (region first, value second) for a map. publish: true makes the URLs live in the same call. A success means it validated AND rendered — look at the preview. Region values that match nothing come back as a 400 listing each with its closest real codes, before anything is made — no separate check needed. `config` is the advanced path: the engine's settings, merged after the knobs.

config.description: ADVANCED: engine settings deep-merged after the knobs

data.description: Typed columns + row-major rows, shaped like the template's example

dateFormat.description: For date columns whose strings are NOT ISO-ish: a strftime-style parse hint tried first — tokens %Y %m %d %b %B %q %H %M %S, e.g. "%d/%m/%Y" for "15/03/2024", "%b %Y" for "Mar 2024". Removes the day/month guess; ISO-ish strings never need it.

type.description: date columns parse ISO-ish strings on their own: "2024", "2024-03", "2024-03-15", "2024-Q2", full ISO timestamps, or epoch numbers. Anything else needs dateFormat.

rows.description: Row-major values, one array per row, order matching columns

knobs.description: The template's knobs — get_template returns their schema

publish.description: true = published and live in this call; omit while you iterate

template.description: Template id or slug from list_templates, or the page address (sweden/municipalities, us/texas/counties, london/wards) when you know the place

name: create_from_template
title: Create a chart from a template with your data and a few knobs — returns an inline preview
